$comment: Published catch-list contexts name the caught failure `error` and mark nothing, because the analyzer used to read the binding by name. `ancestor` places the member: the matched key is the `code` / `data` member of the `error` binding of an `x-telo-context` written beside `x-telo-outcome-list: catches`, so a `code` key anywhere else in a kind's schema is out of reach, and `withoutKey` leaves a member that already carries a mark alone. The third rule gives a published `notFoundHandler.catches` — the one catch list http-server published with no context at all — the context http-server 0.39.1 binds there — `request`, and `error` with `code`, `message` and `data`; `withoutKey: x-telo-context` leaves every list that has one alone.
reason: A catch list's context says which of its members carry the caught failure's code and data with `x-telo-caught-member: code | data`, so a `when:` comparing any marked chain proves coverage and every data-marked member is typed from the codes an entry matches; the analyzer no longer reads a binding named `error`.

host.description: The request's host, lowercased and without its port — from X-Forwarded-Host only behind a trusted proxy.
